impl.summary:
SPEC section 11 is implemented in frontend-v2 only, in 4 commits: c5d8e1a (admin UI), d89e46e (nginx and dev proxy), eeeea89 and 4c99fd7 (tests). Everything that needs the new backend endpoints only runs when the header returns capabilities.refs; otherwise behaviour is as before.

11.1 nginx and dev proxy
- nginx.conf: `set $trajectory_upstream http://${TRAJECTORY_HOST};` plus `location ^~ /api/admin/trajectories/` (same proxy headers as /api/) and `location = /ws/admin/trajectories` (HTTP/1.1, Upgrade/Connection headers, proxy_read_timeout and proxy_send_timeout 3600s). The gzip settings are kept.
- Dockerfile: `ENV TRAJECTORY_HOST=backend:8080`.
- scripts/test-nginx.mjs: adds a `trajectory-worker` fixture upstream on port 8090 and asserts:
  - list, record (`expand=refs`), blob and `meta=1` URLs, and the ticket POST, reach the worker with URI, query and body intact;
  - the WebSocket upgrade on the exact socket path reaches the worker; the rendered config has the 3600 s timeouts;
  - `/api/echo`, `/api/admin/users` and `/ws/fixture` stay on the backend;
  - a frontend started without TRAJECTORY_HOST starts and routes both trajectory paths to the backend;
  - the existing backend IP rotation check still passes.
- vite.config.ts: `/api/admin/trajectories/` and `/ws/admin/trajectories` come before `/api` and `/ws`, targeting VITE_TRAJECTORY_PROXY_TARGET, or the backend when it is unset.

11.2 Admin UI polling (new file constants/polling.ts)
- Events: every 10 s while the socket is connected, every 2 s while it is not, never more often than every 5 s in a hidden tab, and immediately when the tab becomes visible. The schedule resets on socket connect and disconnect.
- Header: every 30 s, and on each watermark hint for the target (at most one read per 5 s, with a trailing read). A hint with `deleted: true` reads the header and polls events at once.
- List probe: every 30 s. Record detail: settles for 2 s on a moving position.

Lazy $ref resolution
- With capabilities.refs, RecordInspector reads details through `trajectoryApi.recordRefs` (`?expand=refs`). Without it, it calls `record()` and the URL is unchanged.
- api/refs.ts reads each reference through `/blobs/{sha256}?through_seq=H`:
  - cached per viewer and session by digest, never re-read once it has content;
  - a 404/410/409 answer is asked again next time;
  - at most 6 reads in flight; nested references are followed; loops and excessive nesting are refused.
- RequestInputPanel, SystemPromptPanel, SystemDiffPanel and ToolCatalogPanel resolve only the fields they display, then render exactly the previous component.
- Every other panel gets the whole record resolved first, so its output is also unchanged.
- ContentActions reads any remaining references before copy or save, and hands nothing out if a read fails or access changes meanwhile.
- New ResolvedRecord component and hook show loading, unavailable (pending/deleted/corrupt/unsupported) and failed-with-retry states. New locale strings (content.loading, failed, preparing, actionFailed) are added in en-US and zh-CN.

Payload revalidation
- With capabilities.refs, a shown payload's bytes are read once. `?meta=1` is then checked every 60 s and when the tab becomes visible; the body (and its Blob) is replaced once the answer is not available or is 404/409/410.
- Without it, the 15 s body refetch is unchanged.

Protocol types
- RefEnvelope and isRefEnvelope, RecordExpand, PayloadMeta, capabilities.refs, TrajectoryWatermark.deleted, and blob, payloadMeta and recordRefs endpoints and query keys.

impl.spec_deviations:
1. Scope of expand=refs. With capabilities.refs, the inspector reads each record detail once with expand=refs for every tab, not only while one of the named components is shown.
   - The four named panels resolve only the $ref values of the fields they display.
   - Every other panel is wrapped in a gate that resolves all references first, so its output is identical to before.
   - Reason: one small detail read per position with immutable per-digest blobs, instead of a fully expanded detail on every tab switch or live refresh.

2. Separate `trajectoryApi.recordRefs()` instead of an expand argument on `record()`.
   - `recordRefs()` sends `?through_seq=H&expand=refs`; the default request sends no expand parameter, so legacy URLs are unchanged.
   - Reason: the existing session-page tests pin `record()`'s positional signature, and lint allows at most 4 parameters.
   - The parameter is carried by the `RecordExpand` type and `useRecordDetail(sessionId, seq, id, { enabled, expand })`.

3. Polling changes are not gated on capabilities.refs; only expand=refs, blob reads and ?meta=1 are.
   - Reason: polling uses no new endpoint, and the list page has no header to read capabilities from.
   - Added a 5 s minimum event-poll interval while the tab is hidden (the spec is silent on hidden tabs; the previous hidden interval was 5 s).

4. "Header refetch on WS hint" is throttled.
   - At most one header read per 5 s since its last answer, with a trailing read so the latest hint is always covered.
   - A hint with `deleted: true` refreshes the header and polls events at once (addition).
   - Reason: a streaming run announces every commit.

5. ?meta=1 details not in the spec.
   - The check also runs when the tab becomes visible (the old body revalidation ran on focus too).
   - Availability other than available/pending/corrupt, including expired and unknown values, hides the body as deleted.
   - A network error on the check keeps the content until the next check.

6. ContentActions resolves references at click time through the shared digest cache. Panels already pass it resolved values, so this path is defensive.

7. nginx: a request to the bare `/api/admin/trajectories` (never used by the SPA) now gets nginx's own 301 to the slash form. This follows from the specified `location ^~ /api/admin/trajectories/`; previously the backend answered 404. test-nginx.mjs pins it. The WS location also carries the Host/X-Real-IP/X-Forwarded-* headers of the existing /ws/ location.

8. Test harness changes.
   - Without FRONTEND_TEST_IMAGE the template runs on stock nginx, so the "started without TRAJECTORY_HOST" container gets the Dockerfile's release-stage ENV defaults, parsed from the Dockerfile (TRAJECTORY_HOST=backend:8080 is asserted). With FRONTEND_TEST_IMAGE the image starts with no env at all.
   - The nginx fixture backend gained QA_PORT and an X-Fixture-Instance header on WebSocket upgrades.

9. Small adaptations: the existing MediaRefView.test.tsx assertion now includes usePayload's new 4th argument ("body"). `src/shared/ws/events.ts` (inside frontend-v2) gained optional `TrajectoryWatermark.deleted`.

10. Resolution limits not in the spec: at most 6 blob reads in flight, 5000 distinct references per value, 8 levels of nested references, 64 container levels. Beyond these the panel says "unsupported" instead of showing partially resolved content.
impl.open_issues:
1. refs mode has vitest coverage only. e2e/helpers/trajectory-server.ts does not return capabilities.refs or serve expand=refs, /blobs or ?meta=1, so Playwright exercised only the legacy path, with the new polling intervals.

2. The UI assumes the wave-2 worker contract from SPEC §8.12:
   - `/blobs/{sha256}?through_seq=H` returns the referenced JSON value itself as the body: 404 not visible or unknown, 410 deleted or expired, 409 corrupt.
   - `/payloads/{id}?meta=1` also accepts through_seq and returns {payload_id, availability, media_type, size_bytes, sha256}.
   - The header sets capabilities.refs=true.
   - Whether expand=refs also leaves $ref values inside record.events is not specified; the gate resolves them if present.

3. Blob answers use TanStack's default gcTime (5 min after the last observer) and are immutable only when they have content. Access purges and target deletion drop them together with the other target keys.

4. Local verification choices: the nginx test used NGINX_TEST_IMAGE=nginx:1.31.5-alpine (amd64-only image here, run under emulation), and Playwright ran on port 3197 via TRAJECTORY_FIXTURE_ORIGIN instead of 3101.

5. Nothing pushed.

verify.head: bd896d3b9823819ad4cfd7057d4f919ce28cba4c
verify.fixes:
I found 5 defects and 1 missing test, and fixed all of them in two commits on top of the implementer's head 4c99fd7: 2a0cb90 (admin UI) and bd896d3 (nginx test). Every changed file is under frontend-v2/. Each new or extended test fails on the implementer's sources: 14 failed across 7 files before the fixes, and they pass after.

1. Reference resolution ran even when the server lacks capabilities.refs (this broke "existing behavior otherwise").
   - Where: the TabPanel gate, the 4 lazy panels and ContentActions resolved `$ref` values whatever the header said.
   - Effect: on today's servers, captured data shaped like `{"$ref":{"sha256":<64 hex>}}` triggered reads of `/blobs/...`. That endpoint does not exist yet, so the panel showed "not produced yet" instead of the data. Every panel render also walked the whole record twice.
   - Fix (useResolvedRecord.ts): `useResolvedValue` returns the value untouched unless `useInspector().refs` is true, and then it walks nothing and makes no queries.
   - Fix (ContentActions.tsx): it checks `useContext(InspectorContext)?.refs === true`, which also works outside an inspector.
   - Tests: a "without capabilities.refs" block in LazyPanels.test.tsx covering all 6 cases (no reads, no queries), plus a check that the summary tab's markup equals SummaryPanel rendered directly. Also new legacy tests in useResolvedRecord.test.tsx and ContentActions.test.tsx, and RecordInspector.test.tsx's legacy test now uses a look-alike and asserts no blob read.

2. A flapping socket could stop event polling entirely.
   - Where: useTrajectorySync reset the poll timer on every `__connected` and `__disconnected`.
   - Effect: the WS client resets its backoff on open. A socket that is accepted and then closed reconnects about every second, so the 2 s poll never fired and the viewer stopped receiving events. The old 1 s poll did not have this problem.
   - Fix: the next read is due a fixed interval after the previous read ended. Socket and visibility changes only re-plan it from that point, and a read in progress is never doubled.
   - Test: a new flapping-socket test in useTrajectorySync.test.tsx (0 polls before the fix, 4 or more after). The existing polling tests still pass unchanged.

3. Hints the header already covered still caused header reads.
   - Where: useHeaderHintRefresh re-read the header for every hint, including the `subscribed` answer on every page open and reconnect. Each open made an extra header read about 5 s later, and each read writes an audit row on the current backend.
   - Fix: a hint whose committed_seq is not newer than the cached header's is skipped. Deletion hints still read at once. The hint type is now `HeaderHint`.
   - Test: a new queries.test.tsx test.

4. The `?meta=1` availability lookup went through the object prototype.
   - Where: `META_AVAILABILITY[meta.availability]` in queries.ts.
   - Effect: a value like "constructor" returned a function, which was stored as the payload's availability.
   - Fix: only own keys of a string value are accepted; anything else hides the content.
   - Test: a new queries.test.tsx test.

5. `resolveValue` (copy and save) never asked again about a cached answer without content.
   - Where: refs.ts. It failed immediately on a cached 404, 410 or 409 answer, which contradicts the documented "asked again next time".
   - Fix: such an answer is fetched once more per call before giving up.
   - Test: a new refs.test.ts test.

6. Missing test: nothing checked that the worker receives the proxy headers.
   - The spec requires the same headers as the `/api/` location, and nothing tested that.
   - The nginx fixture (scripts/fixtures/nginx-backend.py) now echoes Host, X-Real-IP, X-Forwarded-For and X-Forwarded-Proto.
   - test-nginx.mjs now asserts that the worker's HTTP location and watermark socket receive the same values as `/api/` and `/ws/`.

Also, in the same commit as 1-5: prettier formatting on the 3 changed files it flagged, and a stale "1 s poll" comment in sync.ts.

Reviewed and found correct:
- nginx locations: `^~` prefix and exact socket path, 3600 s timeouts, gzip kept.
- Dockerfile ENV default.
- vite.config.ts proxy order.
- `expand=refs` sent only with capabilities.refs; legacy record URLs and query keys unchanged.
- Blob cache keyed by viewer, epoch and digest; cleared by access purge and target deletion.
- Payload meta revalidation.
- Locales: the new keys exist in both, with no duplicate keys.
- The tab list does not depend on resolved data.
- No files outside frontend-v2.

verify.remaining_issues:
1. Refs mode is covered by vitest only. e2e/helpers/trajectory-server.ts does not model capabilities.refs, `expand=refs`, `/blobs` or `?meta=1`, so Playwright exercised only the legacy path.

2. The UI still assumes the wave-2 worker contract:
   - A blob body is the referenced JSON value itself; 404, 410 and 409 mean pending, deleted and corrupt.
   - The meta response shape is `{payload_id, availability, media_type, size_bytes, sha256}`.
   - Open question: whether `expand=refs` also leaves `$payload` envelopes unexpanded. If it does, request input would show a lazily loaded JSON tree instead of expanded data.

3. The polling changes are not gated on capabilities.refs, as the implementer's deviation 3 says. They use existing endpoints, and the list page has no header to gate on. On today's backend, events are polled every 10 s while the socket is connected, instead of every 1 s.

4. `WorkspaceLayout.isolation.test.tsx` ("still connects the viewer's own realtime channel…") is timing-sensitive. It uses a default 1 s waitFor and failed twice in full runs under heavy CPU load (backend pytest running at the same time). It passes alone and in a clean full run, and it is outside this package.

5. ReadingActions (copy or save of a value that still holds references) is defensive code that the current wiring never reaches, because panels pass resolved values. If it were reached, a clipboard write after an await may be refused by browsers without transient user activation (Safari), and `useCopy` has no catch.

6. In meta mode, the payload body query keeps TanStack's default refetch on network reconnect, so bytes are downloaded again after a reconnect. The periodic re-download is gone.

7. `TRAJECTORY_HOST` defaults to `backend:8080` independently of `BACKEND_HOST`, as the spec requires. Any compose or k8s setup that overrides `BACKEND_HOST` must also set `TRAJECTORY_HOST`; that belongs to the w1-ops package.

8. Local choices:
   - The nginx test used `NGINX_TEST_IMAGE=nginx:1.31.5-alpine`, because `nginx:alpine` is not present locally.
   - Playwright ran on port 3219 via `TRAJECTORY_FIXTURE_ORIGIN`.
   - The 39 eslint warnings existed before this package.

9. Nothing was pushed.
